13 — Analytics and Product Metrics Checklist#

Verify that product metrics answer meaningful decisions and are built on well-defined events, trustworthy data, privacy-aware collection, and sound experimentation. This template does not certify that a particular analytics vendor's reports or causal claims are correct.

Scope: Shared / cross-cutting. This file is one part of the 13_Analytics_and_ProductMetrics.md checklist. Apply the domain-wide release gate across all applicable scope files; each checklist ID remains unique.

Review details#

  • Project / product:
  • Release / version / environment:
  • Scope and applicable jurisdictions / markets:
  • Critical product metrics and metric owners:
  • Analytics platforms / tracking plan version:
  • Consent and data-processing review owner:
  • Reviewer / owner:
  • Review date:
  • Decision: Pending / Approved / Approved with documented exceptions / Blocked

How to use#

  1. Copy this shared checklist into a project-specific review; leave all repository checkboxes unchecked.
  2. Mark [x] only after verifying an item using approved metric definitions, a tracking plan, validation tests, reconciliation, representative reports, an experiment design, or authorized privacy decisions. Record failed items and valid N/A rationales in project notes/issues keyed by ANL ID rather than adding evidence tables here.
  3. Tailor measurement to actual product goals and lawful data collection. Not every service uses advertising attribution, browser analytics, monetization funnels, experiments, or GA4.
  4. Review ## API Checks and ## Frontend Checks independently when applicable; document N/A and why for missing product surfaces in project records.
  5. Revalidate after event-schema, consent, attribution, instrumentation, pipeline, identity, or metric-definition changes. Complete detailed Security, Legal, Data Governance, and Experimentation specialist reviews separately where needed.

Measurement strategy and metric definitions#

  • ANL-001 Identify primary product goals and the user behaviors that demonstrate progress toward each goal.
  • ANL-002 Define a concise North Star or comparable primary outcome metric only where it meaningfully reflects customer value.
  • ANL-003 Assign an accountable business owner and a technical measurement owner to every critical product metric.
  • ANL-004 Write a metric dictionary with numerator, denominator, eligible population, time window, units, data source, and calculation logic.
  • ANL-005 Specify how active users, sessions, new users, conversions, orders, and retained users are defined before comparing reports.
  • ANL-006 Document user and account identity semantics, anonymous identifiers, and the rules for connecting sessions across devices when allowed.
  • ANL-007 Distinguish user-level, account-level, session-level, event-level, and transaction-level metrics to avoid denominator mistakes.
  • ANL-009 Define acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, monetization, and referral metrics only when relevant to the product.
  • ANL-010 Record baselines, expected ranges, targets, measurement frequency, and owners for important outcomes.
  • ANL-011 Establish the cohort entry event, eligibility window, observation period, and retention calculation for cohort analyses.
  • ANL-012 Document what counts as successful task completion and how abandoned, retried, failed, and partial transactions are treated.
  • ANL-013 Define attribution windows and rules for organic, paid, referral, direct, and unknown acquisition sources when relevant.
  • ANL-014 Identify limitations introduced by consent, blockers, offline use, cross-device identity, and missing events before making comparisons.
  • ANL-015 Ensure monetary metrics distinguish gross/net amounts, refunds, currencies, taxes, discounts, and exchange-rate conversions where applicable.
  • ANL-016 Define whether metrics are observed, sampled, modeled, estimated, or derived and label dashboards accordingly.
  • ANL-017 Plan segmentation by platform, cohort, geography, customer tier, and accessibility-relevant user experience where justified and lawful.
  • ANL-018 Check that dashboards distinguish operational health metrics from user or business outcome metrics.
  • ANL-019 Record known risks of survivorship bias, selection bias, changing populations, and seasonality for major analyses.
  • ANL-020 Review the metric definitions with product, engineering, analytics, privacy, and finance owners as applicable.
  • ANL-021 Define escalation and correction procedures when a key metric's business meaning or computation changes.
  • ANL-022 Use a decision log tying metric movements and experiments to actual product or investment decisions.

Event taxonomy and implementation#

  • ANL-023 Maintain an approved tracking plan mapping each important user journey and business question to the events needed to answer it.

  • ANL-024 Define event names, descriptions, trigger conditions, owner, platform, and implementation source before instrumenting them.

  • ANL-025 Use consistent event naming and case conventions, avoiding reserved names and vendor-specific limits when a chosen tool has them.

  • ANL-026 Document event parameters with types, units, allowed values, nullability, and examples.

  • ANL-028 Identify authoritative events for high-impact transactions rather than counting unverified button clicks as completed purchases.

  • ANL-029 Distinguish auto-collected, recommended, and custom events in a vendor implementation and avoid unintentional duplication.

  • ANL-031 Verify one logical user action does not create multiple identical conversion events unless multiple outcomes are intended.

  • ANL-032 Decide how event timestamps, ingestion timestamps, time zones, and late-arriving events are represented.

  • ANL-033 Define the lifecycle of anonymous, authenticated, and account identities, including logout and account switching.

  • ANL-034 Use stable event or transaction identifiers for deduplication and reconciliation where appropriate.

  • ANL-035 Capture campaign/referrer attribution fields consistently without including secrets or personal query parameters.

  • ANL-036 Document what happens when users decline measurement, disable storage, or revoke consent in applicable products.

  • ANL-037 Include source app/platform, environment, and release version so data from tests and production can be separated.

  • ANL-043 Review event instrumentation for performance overhead and avoid blocking critical user interactions on analytics delivery.

  • ANL-044 Treat the tracking plan as a maintained contract, updating it in the same release workflow as affected product behavior.

Data quality and reporting#

  • ANL-045 Reconcile critical conversions and financial totals against a trusted transactional system rather than assuming analytics collection is complete.

  • ANL-049 Document the treatment of bots, internal testers, QA traffic, employee accounts, and automated probes in reporting.

  • ANL-050 Verify users, sessions, and conversion deduplication rules against representative edge cases.

  • ANL-051 Test metric calculations against small hand-verified examples, including dates, partial periods, and timezone boundaries.

  • ANL-052 Check that revenue and currency conversion calculations use documented rounding and exchange-rate rules.

  • ANL-053 Document report sampling, thresholding, modeling, export limits, and attribution differences of the selected analytics provider.

  • ANL-054 Verify raw-data export frequency and completeness meet dashboard expectations; do not assume streaming exports contain finalized attribution.

  • ANL-055 Define whether late and corrected events trigger recomputation, backfill, or permanent historical limitations.

  • ANL-056 Audit join keys and identity stitching to prevent multiplying events through many-to-many warehouse joins.

  • ANL-057 Use consistent cohort, date, audience, environment, and currency filters in comparisons that are meant to reconcile.

  • ANL-058 Verify tracking between consented and non-consented users is handled legally and that any resulting measurement gaps are disclosed.

  • ANL-059 Use appropriate row-level controls or aggregation for sensitive reporting dimensions, especially low-count cohorts.

  • ANL-060 Document the canonical dashboard or semantic model for each metric to reduce conflicting versions of the truth.

  • ANL-061 Include units, owner, source, last refresh, applied filters, and confidence or caveat annotations on important dashboards.

  • ANL-062 Restrict edit and publish rights for production dashboards, metric definitions, and business-critical transformations.

  • ANL-063 Provide a process for responding to metric anomalies and retroactive corrections, including downstream communication.

  • ANL-066 Record the known reporting gaps, unsupported segments, and historical discontinuities that affect business decisions.

Privacy, consent, and data lifecycle#

  • ANL-068 Document why each collected field is necessary and remove unnecessary or disproportionately sensitive attributes.
  • ANL-069 Determine applicable consent, lawful-basis, transparency, and tracking-technology rules with qualified privacy reviewers.
  • ANL-070 Ensure storage/access technologies follow the applicable rules before non-essential collection or access begins.
  • ANL-071 Verify analytics and advertising purposes are not silently bundled when the applicable consent framework requires separate choices.
  • ANL-073 Check analytics collection after logout, account switching, and consent withdrawal for unintended identifiers or linkage.
  • ANL-074 Prevent passwords, authentication tokens, payment details, health information, and other prohibited sensitive values from appearing in analytics payloads.
  • ANL-075 Review URL, referrer, search-query, form, and error-message fields for accidental personal-data collection.
  • ANL-076 Use appropriately scoped pseudonymous identifiers and documented reidentification controls where tracking is justified.
  • ANL-077 Restrict access to user-level event data, exports, dashboards, and third-party accounts by role and actual business need.
  • ANL-078 Apply documented retention periods and deletion rules to event stores, identity maps, exports, and derived tables as required.
  • ANL-079 Define how correction, access, and erasure requests affect analytics identifiers and derived records when applicable.
  • ANL-080 Review cross-border transfers and external processor arrangements where the applicable legal framework requires it.
  • ANL-081 Assess whether consent gaps, privacy filters, and signal loss make certain cohorts unrepresentative.
  • ANL-082 Validate that debug instrumentation and staging environments do not send real user data into inappropriate production analytics properties.
  • ANL-083 Document data-subject or customer inquiries and who responds to analytics-related privacy requests.
  • ANL-084 Reassess the privacy impact when adding advertising identifiers, cross-device tracking, new third parties, or sensitive segments.
  • ANL-085 Keep public notices and internal data maps aligned with the actual tools, data fields, and processing purposes.

Experimentation and decision quality#

  • ANL-086 State an experiment hypothesis and the intended user or business behavior change before allocating users.
  • ANL-088 Define randomization unit, audience eligibility, targeting, allocation, and assignment persistence.
  • ANL-090 Choose a control group or suitable counterfactual rather than treating before/after movement as automatic proof of causality.
  • ANL-091 Confirm exposure events are emitted for the intended population and linked to metric events through the correct identity key.
  • ANL-092 Monitor sample-ratio mismatch and investigate persistent imbalance before trusting experiment comparisons.
  • ANL-093 Check crossover, unexpected reassignments, missing exposures, and unequal event loss across variants.
  • ANL-094 Define an analysis window and rules for multiple comparisons, repeated looks, and early stopping appropriate to the methodology.
  • ANL-095 Distinguish statistical uncertainty from practical significance and report effect sizes with uncertainty estimates when supported.
  • ANL-096 Monitor reliability, accessibility, user-harm, privacy, and business guardrails during experiment rollout.
  • ANL-097 Specify when an experiment must be paused because of safety, severe regressions, or data-quality failures.
  • ANL-098 Document platform, device, cohort, and geographic segments selected in advance to avoid overinterpreting post hoc subgroups.
  • ANL-101 Record experiment conclusions, metric caveats, decision owners, and whether a result justified launch, iteration, or abandonment.
  • ANL-102 Do not present observational correlations, dashboard fluctuations, or statistically invalid experiments as causal evidence.
  • ANL-103 Retain the analysis specification and relevant variant/version details to make major decisions reproducible.
  • ANL-104 Reassess experiments when tracking implementations, audience eligibility, or key metric definitions change during the test.

Release gate#

  • Launch-critical business and user outcome metrics have stable definitions, owners, targets or baselines, and documented measurement limitations.
  • Critical events have an approved tracking plan, unique trigger semantics, appropriate identity and attribution rules, and validated representative client/server payloads.
  • Key conversion, transactional, or financial metrics reconcile with the authoritative system to an agreed tolerance, or material gaps have an accepted remediation plan.
  • Applicable consent, notices, data minimization, privacy controls, recipient access, and retention requirements have been reviewed and approved by the appropriate owner.
  • Analytics ingestion and dashboards are checked for freshness, missing events, duplicates, inappropriate test traffic, and known export or modeling limits.
  • Any launch-critical experiment has a documented hypothesis, decision metrics, randomization/health checks, and approved stop or rollout rules.
  • Responsible API/frontend owners confirm that relevant user journeys are measured correctly without disrupting functionality or collecting prohibited sensitive data.
  • Unresolved defects that could materially mislead product decisions, harm users, or breach applicable data-processing requirements have an owner, escalation path, and explicit authorized disposition.

Domain-specific approval rule: Do not approve measurement as release-ready when critical decisions depend on undefined or demonstrably incorrect metrics, required consent/collection rules are unaddressed, server-side business events systematically double count, or invalid experiment allocation is used to claim causality. Analytics review is not a substitute for legal/privacy compliance review or independent financial audit.

Trusted references and scope#

These checks translate source guidance into testable measurement and decision controls. Vendor-specific technical details apply only when that platform is used; these references are not a universal compliance standard.

  • Google Analytics — Set up events — user interaction event design, collection, and verification.
  • Google Analytics — Recommended events — established event semantics and prescribed parameters for applicable use cases.
  • Google Analytics — Event naming rules — naming restrictions, case sensitivity, and reserved names for GA4.
  • Google Analytics — Measurement Protocol — server-side/offline events and their intended supplementary use.
  • Google Analytics — Validate Measurement Protocol events — payload validation and the difference between transport success and accepted events.
  • Google Analytics — BigQuery Export — export timeliness, completeness, attribution limitations, and sampling differences.
  • Google Tag Platform — Consent mode on websites — technically honoring recorded consent choices for Google tags, where used.
  • UK ICO — Final storage and access technologies guidance announcement (2026) — current UK regulatory context for cookies and analogous tracking technologies where applicable.
  • Microsoft PlayFab — Experiment best practices — experiment health, sample-ratio mismatch, and unbiased interpretation.
  • Statsig — Experiment health monitoring — exposure consistency, sample ratio, and guardrail checks in experiments.
  • Statsig — Experiment decision framework — predefined primary and guardrail metrics, decisions, and reviews.
  • Statsig — Experiment overview — randomization and causal inference principles for controlled experiments.

Applicability: GA4 event names, API payload limits, and BigQuery export semantics are relevant only to GA4 implementations. UK tracking obligations depend on applicable law and current regulatory guidance, including changes made in 2026; seek qualified legal advice for jurisdiction-specific decisions. Online controlled experiments should be used only when methodologically appropriate. Consent-driven gaps, identity uncertainty, ad blockers, and sampling can affect measurement completeness and must not be ignored.

Source review date: 2026-11-12.

Suggested testing tools#

Choose tools appropriate to the project's stack and risks; automation supports evidence but does not approve the checklist.

  • Test focus: event naming, consent, schemas, experiments, and reporting integrity; include shared/cross-team controls where applicable.
  • Cross-stack: GA4 DebugView.
  • Python: Pandera + pytest; for pytest-based suites, run python -m pytest -q.
  • TypeScript: Zod + Vitest; for Vitest-based suites, run npx vitest run (or npx playwright test for E2E).
  • JavaScript: Ajv + Jest; for Jest-based suites, run npx jest --ci (or npx playwright test for E2E).
  • Evidence: Save tool versions, configuration, test environment, fixtures, results, and links in project-specific review records using the existing checklist IDs. Expert review remains necessary where relevant.

Suggested AI skills for verification#

These are optional agent review aids, not automated passes or release approval. Each linked repository had at least 1,000 GitHub stars when checked on 2026-11-12; counts are per repository, not per skill, and do not indicate security or correctness.

  • analytics — Review event data and measurement plans (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).
  • ab-testing — Assess experiment controls and results (coreyhaines31/marketingskills, 59,899 repo stars).
  • kpi-dashboard-design — Check metric definitions and dashboards (wshobson/agents, 42,437 repo stars).

How to check: In a project-specific copy, have the agent audit the shared / cross-cutting scope and map findings to this file's existing checklist IDs, with code/configuration references, reproducible test results, failed or inapplicable cases, and uncertainties. Independently verify findings; keep shared template boxes unchecked and retain human approval requirements.

Before use: Read the skill's SKILL.md, referenced scripts, license, and requested tool permissions. Only execute vetted skills with appropriate access in a controlled environment.

Important warning: reference only#

⚠️ Reference only — not a definitive or exhaustive checklist. This template is a starting point for review, not the ultimate authority or a guarantee of project safety, quality, regulatory compliance, accessibility, security, or launch readiness.

Use project-specific judgment and independent verification. Requirements and risks evolve and differ by project, technology, and jurisdiction. Adapt the checks, consult current authoritative sources, perform relevant tests, and obtain qualified specialist review or approval when appropriate. Checking every box does not replace these steps.

Reference, not a certification. Check applicability, verify important claims against current primary sources, and seek expert review where necessary. Suggest an improvement.
